items.text: More than 70 million people worldwide stutter , which is about one percent of the global population. Five percent of all children go through a period of stuttering, and most recover by late childhood. However, some have a long-term stutter, and scientists still don’t fully understand why. They studied the brains of people who stutter or who recovered from a stutter; they found they are different from the brains of people who don’t. This study means that a stutter has a neurological origin, and it comes from genetic differences. The condition often runs in families, and some of the genetic differences are related to sex. Men are more likely to stutter as children and more likely to continue to stutter into adulthood. The treatment of stutter differs and depends on whether the person is a young child very close to onset , a school-aged child, or an adult. Some techniques can help reduce the stutter; however, they don’t fix the neurological differences. Therapies help people understand that what they say is far more important than how they say it. However, society isn’t always accepting and supportive. Difficult words: stutter (to speak with difficulty, for example, to pause before saying a word or repeat it several times), neurological (related to the brain and the nervous system), onset (the beginning of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Reports say that 70 million people worldwide stutter. This is about one percent of the whole population. People who stutter have problems when they speak. Usually, they make a pause before they say a difficult word, or they repeat the same word several times. Scientists found that these people have different brains, so you cannot always stop a stutter. More people in one family often stutter, so the condition is genetic , too. Interestingly, men stutter three times more than women, but scientists don’t really know why. People can learn some techniques , which make their stutter less obvious , but these techniques don’t change the brain. They learn to understand that what we speak is more important rather than how we say. Difficult words: genetic (genes or information in the body that pass from one parents to children), techniques (the way to do something), obvious (something that people can see). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people stutter. A stutter changes how they speak. Sometimes they cannot say some words. Sometimes they repeat the same word more times. Or they make pauses when they speak. More than 70 million people stutter in all world. Five percent of children stutter at some time in their lives. Most of them stop. Some people stutter all life. Scientists say that these people have different brains. The situation is very difficult to change. Also, more people in the same family stutter. It is common . Men stutter more often than women. People learn some techniques to speak better. They must understand that they can’t change their brain. Also, they must understand that what you say is more important than how you say it. Difficult words: pause (the time between two actions), common (usual), technique (how people do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite the popularity of action titles like Fortnite or GTA, survival horror continues to attract loyal fans. At Gamescom in Germany, players explained that these games offer not only fear but also atmosphere, responsibility, and emotional stories. Developers agreed that horror must constantly evolve to keep audiences interested. Silent Hill F takes the series to 1960s Japan, adding cultural strangeness and focusing on psychological terror. Written by the Japanese author Ryukishi07, it emphasizes mystery and inner fear rather than fast action. This design avoids turning the game into a typical combat challenge, instead highlighting tension and emotional impact. Resident Evil Requiem marks the 30th anniversary of the franchise . It returns to Raccoon City, offering improved graphics, two camera modes, and a vulnerable main character named Grace. Developers stressed that their goal is to create horror-first experiences, not action-first ones, showing that survival horror still has a strong identity. Difficult words: evolve (to change slowly into something better), emphasize (to give importance to something), franchise (a series of games, movies, or books that belong to the same world or story). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Survival horror games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill are still strong, even with famous action games around. At Gamescom, fans said they like these games because they give fear, atmosphere, and strong stories. Developers said they need to add new ideas but keep the spirit of horror alive. Silent Hill F moves the game into 1960s Japan. It brings a new culture and focuses more on the mind than on action. The story comes from writer Ryukishi07, who is known for dark stories. Resident Evil Requiem celebrates 30 years of the series. It shows Raccoon City again, has better graphics , two ways to play (first-person and third-person), and a normal woman named Grace as the hero . The creators want horror to stay the main point. Difficult words: spirit (the main idea or feeling of something), graphics (the pictures, images, or visuals in a game or on screen), hero (the main good character in a story). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some players love survival horror games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill. At Gamescom in Germany, fans say that these games are scary and exciting . They also say that the games tell good stories. The makers want to keep the fear but also give new ideas. Silent Hill F is in Japan in the 1960s. It is not about fast fighting. It is more about strange feelings and scary thoughts . Resident Evil Requiem is 30 years old now. The game shows Raccoon City again. It has better pictures and two ways to play. The main person is a woman called Grace. The makers say that horror must stay the most important part of the game. Difficult words: exciting (something what makes you feel happy, interested, or full of energy), fear (the strong feeling when you think that something is dangerous or scary), thought (an idea in your mind). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bottled water is a convenient product when you need a quick drink; however, where is it made, and why does it cost so much? Tap water isn’t a universal luxury . It’s estimated that more than 800 million people around the world don’t have safe drinking water, and even in the US, cities had to use bottled water instead of tap water. The tap water had aging facilities or toxic chemicals in the water supply. Bottled water isn’t better or cleaner than tap water. Tap water has more laws than bottled water; however, bottled water costs more. Bottled water has a huge environmental impact. It usually comes from a lake, spring, or underground aquifer , and on average, manufacturers need 3 liters of water to make one liter of bottled water. To make plastic bottles, they need billions of gallons of oil every year and 2,000 times more energy than tap water needs. Difficult words: convenient (useful to a purpose), universal luxury (something that everyone has and is pleasant), aquifer (a layer of rock, sand, or Earth that contains water). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Around 800 million of people around the world have no access to safe water to drink. For many others, it is a normal thing. Bottled water is the most popular drink in the US, but many problems come with the drink. Some cities have only bottled water, as the pipes for tap water are too old. Bottled water is much more expensive than tap water. At the same time, tap water is safer, and bottled water has a very bad impact on the natural world. A factory usually needs three liters of water to make one liter of bottled water. Also, to make bottles, it is necessary to burn oil. To make bottled water requires 2,000 times more energy than tap water requires. Difficult words: access (the right or possibility to have something), tap (a device through which water comes in homes), require (to need). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people in the world have safe water to drink. Around 800 million people have no safe water to drink. Some people can normally buy water in a plastic bottle. Bottled water is the most popular drink in the US. This water is not better than water from a tap . It is much more expensive. It is much worse for the natural world. Companies need three liters of water to make one liter of bottled water. They also must burn oil to make the bottles. Bottled water needs much more energy than water from a tap. Difficult words: bottled (in a bottle), popular (something that many people like), tap (a device through which water comes in homes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Argentina, five foals have become the world’s first gene-edited horses, created by Kheiron Biotech using CRISPR technology. Unlike cloning, which produces identical copies, CRISPR allows scientists to cut and change DNA. In this case, they reduced the myostatin gene, which normally limits muscle growth, to create horses with stronger muscles and faster speed. Supporters argue this could transform polo breeding. However, the Argentine Polo Association has banned gene-edited horses from competition, saying they harm the tradition and magic of natural breeding. Many breeders worry about unfair advantages and possible economic risks if international buyers reject GE horses. Others compare the technology to artificial intelligence, claiming it reduces the role of human skill. Despite controversy , Argentina has a history of adopting biotechnology, from cloning to embryo transfers. Experts believe that science will continue to advance, though for now, the future of gene-edited polo horses remains uncertain. Time will show whether they truly outperform naturally bred animals. Difficult words: foal (a young horse), controversy (public disagreement), outperform (do better than someone or something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Argentina produced the world’s first gene-edited horses using a tool that changes DNA. Scientists reduced a gene that slows muscle growth, hoping to create faster and stronger horses. The company Kheiron Biotech says this can revolutionize polo breeding . But the Argentine Polo Association doesn’t let these horses compete. Leaders say polo should keep its natural style, where breeders choose horses to breed. Some breeders also worry that buyers from other countries may not accept GE horses. Argentina already uses cloning and other science in horse breeding, so some people believe gene-editing is only the next step, but others fear it changes too much. For now, the sport is waiting to see if these horses will really do better than other horses. Difficult words: gene-edited (when scientists change the DNA of a living thing to give it special qualities), revolutionize (to change completely), breed (to raise animals for special qualities). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Argentina, five new horses are very special. They are the first gene-edited horses in the world. Scientists use a tool called CRISPR to change their DNA. They make the horses grow more muscle, so they can be faster. The company Kheiron Biotech believes that this is a big step for polo. But the Argentine Polo Association says no. These horses cannot play polo games. They want the sport to stay natural , with normal breeding . Some people are afraid that other countries will not buy these new horses. In the past, Argentina already used science like cloning. Some people like new ideas, but others do not. Nobody knows yet if these horses are really better. Difficult words: gene-edited (when scientists change the DNA of a living thing to give it special qualities), natural (something that happens by itself in nature, without changes by people), breeding (producing young animals by carefully choosing parents). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US retirement system received a C+ grade in the Mercer CFA Institute 2024 Global Pension Index, behind countries such as the Netherlands and Australia. Experts say the American system suffers from low participation, voluntary contributions, and frequent early withdrawals, known as 401(k) leakage. This weakens long-term savings and puts Social Security, already expected to face insolvency by 2033, under greater pressure. Americans often take money out early to pay for emergencies, houses, or health care, which reduces compound interest growth. Other nations require mandatory contributions and higher retirement ages to adapt to people living longer. The Netherlands is praised for strong governance and compulsory contributions. By contrast, in the US, participation in retirement plans is voluntary, and many workers choose not to opt in . Still, the US has some strengths: high average retirement incomes and Social Security’s progressive formula . Experts argue reforms like limiting leakage and boosting contributions could raise the country’s grade. Difficult words: insolvency (not having enough money to pay debts), compound (when something grows by adding more to itself, for example, interest on money), opt in (to agree or join something by one’s own decision), formula (a set rule or system for calculation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US retirement system got a C+ grade in 2024, lower than countries like the Netherlands or Australia. Experts explain that the US has problems with low participation , voluntary savings, and early withdrawals . Many Americans take their money out before retirement to pay for emergencies or houses, which reduces their savings. Social Security is also in trouble and may not have enough money by 2033. In other countries, such as the Netherlands, people have to contribute to the retirement system, which helps create strong savings for workers. In the US, it is voluntary, so many people don’t join. Even so, the US has high retirement incomes compared to many countries. Experts believe new rules and reforms could improve the system. Difficult words: participation (taking part in something), voluntary (something you do because you want to, not because you must), withdrawal (taking money out). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US retirement system is not very strong. In 2024, it gets a C+ grade. Other countries, for example, the Netherlands, do better. One problem is that people in the US do not always join retirement plans. Another problem is that they take their money out early. Many workers take money from accounts before retirement, for health, houses, or other needs. This makes their savings smaller. Social Security may also have problems with money by 2033. In other countries, workers must put money into the retirement system, so they save more. In the US, it is a choice , not a rule. Even so, many Americans have good retirement incomes . Experts say that new changes could make the system stronger. Difficult words: retirement system (the way a country or company organizes money for people when they stop working), income (the money you get, usually from work or investments), choice (something you choose to do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The first World Humanoid Robot Games were held in Beijing, with participants from 16 countries, including the US, Germany, and Japan. Robots competed in events such as athletics, football, dance, and martial arts. The competition was not only entertainment but also a way to test and improve robots’ decision-making, motor skills , and control systems that could later be applied in industries and homes. China aims to become a global leader in humanoid robotics and has set a goal of developing a world-class industry by 2027. While the Games attracted international teams, they also served as a large-scale promotion for China’s robotics sector, which has received billions of dollars in investment. The event demonstrated both the challenges and potential of humanoid robots, from technical failures to impressive performances. Supporters argue that humanoid designs make it easier for robots to function in human environments, though critics question the need to copy human forms. For China, winning recognition and attracting investment may determine which robotics companies survive in this highly competitive field. Difficult words: motor skills (the ability to control and coordinate your body’s movements), recognition (knowing someone or something because you saw or heard it before), competitive (involving rivalry between participants). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Beijing hosted the first World Humanoid Robot Games with teams from 16 countries, including the US, Germany, and Japan. Robots took part in sports such as running, football, dance, and martial arts. The goal was not just fun but also to test robots’ skills, such as movement, decision-making , and control, which could later help in factories and homes. China wants to become a world leader in humanoid robotics and has a plan to build this industry by 2027. Although some foreign teams joined, the event was also a way to promote China’s robot industry. Companies invest billions of dollars in robots, but not all of them will succeed . Supporters say making robots look human helps them fit better into daily life, while critics ask why robots must look like people at all. Difficult words: decision-making (choosing between different options or actions), promote (to advertise or support something), succeed (to do well or win). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The first World Humanoid Robot Games happen in Beijing, China. Teams from 16 countries, like the US, Germany, and Japan, join. Robots try different sports, such as running, football, dance, and fighting. The event is also a test to see how robots move, think, and work. This can help robots be useful in places like factories and homes. China wants to be the world leader in robots by 2027. The Games are fun, but also very serious for companies. Many people are giving money to robot businesses, but not all will win. Some people say that robots should look like humans so they can work better in our world. Others say that robots could look like anything. Difficult words: event (something that happens), serious (important and not funny), human (a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chinese pianist Lang Lang gave a piano performance at Jungfraujoch, the highest railway station in Europe. The artist wished to promote cultural exchanges between China and Europe with music. At a height of 4,158 meters above the sea, Jungfraujoch is a famous scenic spot and snow sports resort. It is also an important summit of the Bernese Alps in central Switzerland. Lang said it was the first time he had played the piano on a snowy mountain, and it was a very special experience, despite the challenging low temperature. Lang’s interpretation of ‘Love dream’, ‘Jasmine flower’, and ‘Goldberg variations’ won warm applause from the audience. Lang specially chose the song ‘Jasmine flower’ in hope the audience would want to learn about Chinese culture through beautiful oriental music. Difficult words: scenic (beautiful natural surroundings), interpretation (a particular way of performing something), oriental (relating to the countries of East and Southeast Asia). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chinese pianist Lang Lang played at Jungfraujoch, the highest railway station in Europe. The performance happened 4,158 meters above the sea level in the Swiss Alps. The cold weather made out hard for the pianist to play, but Lang said that it was a very special moment for him. He enjoyed the beautiful scenery . People enjoyed Lang’s performance very much. He played three songs to interest people in Asian music. Lang said that he would like to support cultural exchange between China and Europe. Difficult words: performance (when an artist sings, plays or dances in front of people), scenery (a beautiful place, especially the nature), exchange (when you give and get something back). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lang Lang is a Chinese pianist. He plays in the Bernese Alps in Switzerland. The Bernese Alps are very tall mountains. Lang Lang plays at 4,158 meters at Jungfraujoch. The highest railway station in Europe is there. It is very cold there. It is not good for a pianist. His fingers are cold. Happily, Lang Lang enjoys the performance very much. The view from the mountain is beautiful. Lang Lang plays three songs. He wants people to be interested in Asian music. He also wants to help the European and Chinese cultures get closer. Difficult words: performance (when an artist sings, plans, or dances in front of people), view (what somebody can see from a place), culture (the food, arts, ideas, and other things of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Several European countries will suspend postal services to the United States after President Donald Trump removed a tax exemption on imported goods worth under 800 dollars, or 682 euros. The US government says the decision is meant to stop illegal practices, such as drug trafficking, but European postal operators argue they received no time to adapt. While letters and small parcels under 85 euros are not affected, most merchandise shipments will stop. Germany, Denmark, Sweden, and Italy have already suspended services, with France, Austria, and the UK set to follow. Postal companies, including La Poste, Deutsche Post, and Correos, say the lack of clear technical details from the US makes it impossible to comply with the new rules. Spain described the halt as a preventive measure to avoid delivery problems. The change will affect transatlantic e-commerce, especially small and medium-sized businesses that depend on exporting low-value products to the US. All commercial shipments will face tariffs starting August 29. Difficult words: suspend (to stop for a period of time), exemption (a rule that lets you avoid a tax or law), merchandise (goods or products for sale). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Europe will stop sending many parcels to the United States because of a new tax rule. US President Donald Trump cancelled a tax exemption for goods under 682 euros. The White House says the change is to fight crime and stop illegal goods, but many European postal companies say the new system is unclear. People can still send small letters and parcels under 85 euros. Germany, Denmark, Sweden, and Italy already stopped deliveries, and France, Austria, and the UK will stop next week. Spain said it must protect customers from delays. The change will make it harder for small businesses in Europe to sell products to the US, because all packages will now have to pay extra taxes. Difficult words: parcel (a box or a package you send in the post), exemption (a rule which keeps you away from paying a tax), goods (things for sale). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many European countries will not send parcels to the United States. The reason is a new tax rule. US President Donald Trump stops a rule which makes small goods free of tax if they cost under 682 euros. Now almost all parcels must pay new taxes. Letters and small parcels under 85 euros can still go. Germany, Sweden, Denmark, and Italy already stop sending parcels. France, Austria, and the UK will stop soon. Spain says the stop is to keep customers from problems. The change is bad for small European shops. They sell cheap products to the US, but now it will cost more money. Difficult words: parcel (a box which you send in the post), tax (money which you must pay to the government), customer (a person who buys things or services from a shop or business). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

North Korea has opened the Wonsan Kalma Coastal Tourist Zone, a resort on the country’s east coast. The area includes hotels, restaurants, shops, and a water park. Originally, the country advertised it as open to international visitors, but so far, only Russians, arriving in organised groups through accredited travel agencies, have been allowed in. Russian tourists who visited said they were impressed by the beach, the quality of the resort, and the hosts’ efforts to meet their requests, although they also mentioned restrictions. Experts say North Korea is opening the resort because it urgently needs foreign currency such as dollars, euros, or rubles. Before the COVID-19 pandemic, Chinese tourists visited in large numbers, but now only a few hundred Russians arrive each month, far fewer than before. Some analysts also suggest the project aims to show off North Korea’s ties with Russia and prove it can offer a world-class holiday destination despite being largely closed to the outside world. Difficult words: accredited (officially approved), host (a person or company who entertains other people as guests), show off (to display someone or something that is a source of pride). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

North Korea has opened a new holiday area called the Wonsan Kalma Coastal Tourist Zone. It has hotels, shops, restaurants, and even a water park. The resort was planned for international tourists, but right now, only Russians can visit it. They come in groups organised by official travel companies. Russian visitors said the beach was beautiful and the resort was good, but there were still many rules. North Korea hopes the project will bring in money. The country needs foreign money like euros, dollars, or rubles. In the past, many Chinese people visited, but since COVID-19, only a few hundred Russians arrive each month. Experts believe North Korea also wants to show its friendship with Russia and prove it can welcome tourists. Difficult words: resort (a place for holidays), foreign (from another country), prove (to show that something is true or possible). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

North Korea has a new holiday place called the Wonsan Kalma Coastal Tourist Zone. It has hotels, restaurants, shops, and a water park. At first, the plan is to open the resort for people from many countries, but now only Russian groups can go. They must come with special travel companies. Russian visitors say that the beach is nice and the place looks good. But they also say that there are many rules for tourists. North Korea wants tourists to bring money. Before COVID, many Chinese people come, but now only a few Russians visit. The country needs money in euros, dollars, or rubles. Experts say that North Korea also wants to show that it is strong and friendly with Russia. Difficult words: holiday (time to rest and travel), resort (a place for holidays), rule (what you can and cannot do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The United Nations has confirmed famine in Gaza City and nearby areas, calling it a “failure of humanity.” UN Secretary-General António Guterres described it as a man-made disaster. A UN-backed group, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), placed Gaza at Phase 5, the most severe level of hunger, where more than half a million people are facing catastrophic conditions, including starvation and death. The IPC warns that without an immediate large-scale response, famine-related deaths will rise. Israel has strongly rejected the report, calling it an outright lie and denying the existence of famine. However, more than 100 humanitarian groups, UN bodies, and several of Israel’s allies say aid is restricted. Aid workers and witnesses on the ground describe extreme suffering, high food prices, and children dying from malnutrition . The famine in Gaza is the first confirmed by the IPC outside Africa. The UN says it was preventable and blames systematic obstruction of aid. The crisis continues without a ceasefire. Difficult words: starvation (suffering or death caused by lack of food), malnutrition (serious illness from not having enough healthy food), obstruction (the act of blocking or stopping something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The United Nations says there is famine in Gaza City and the surrounding areas. António Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, called it a man-made disaster . A special food security group (IPC) says more than 500,000 people in Gaza are living in very dangerous conditions. Many families face hunger, sickness, and even death. The group warns that the situation will get worse if more food and help don’t arrive quickly. People in Gaza describe very high food prices, hunger, and children dying. The UN says that people made this situation because help came too late. Israel disagrees and calls the report a lie. It says there is no famine. But many UN groups, aid workers, and even Israel’s allies say the help going into Gaza is not enough. Difficult words: famine (no food for many people), disaster (a serious and dangerous situation), ally (a country or person who helps and supports another one in a difficult situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The United Nations says that there is famine in Gaza. Famine means that people do not have enough food. Many families are hungry . The situation is serious. Some people are sick. Some children die because they cannot eat. The UN says that more than 500,000 people have a problem with food. Israel says this is not true . It says that there is no famine. But many helpers and UN groups say that food does not get to Gaza as it should. They say that people need more help, and they need it faster. The UN leader says that people are responsible for this situation. It is very bad news for the world. Help comes too late. Difficult words: famine (no food for many people), hungry (when you want food), true (real). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After eight years of preparation and a cost of over 44 million euros, the famous Kiruna Kyrka church in northern Sweden has begun its unusual journey. The red wooden church, built in 1912 and weighing 672 tonnes, is being slowly rolled 5km to a new location at a speed of half a kilometre per hour. The move is part of a large, decades-long relocation of the whole Arctic town of Kiruna, which is threatened by the expansion of Europe’s biggest underground iron ore mine. Thousands of people, including Sweden’s king, are expected to watch as the church makes its way through specially widened streets. The event is broadcast live, turning it into a kind of national spectacle . The church is valued not only for its age but also for its design, which resembles a traditional Sámi hut. However, the project has received criticism. Members of the Sámi community argue that the mining company is destroying land and culture, making reindeer herding and traditional life increasingly difficult. Difficult words: relocation (moving something to a new place), spectacle (a public event that many people watch), resemble (to look like). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In northern Sweden, the town of Kiruna is moving a famous church called Kiruna Kyrka. The church is very old, and it looks like a Sámi hut . People built it in 1912, and it weighs 672 tonnes. The church will travel 5km to a new home. The reason is that the land under the town is not safe, because a very large iron ore mine is making the ground weaker. The move of the church is part of a big plan to move most of the town. Many people are interested in this event. The Swedish king and thousands of others will watch the church travel slowly, half a kilometre each hour. People across the country can also watch the move on TV. The project costs more than 44 million euros. Some Sámi people are not happy. They say the mine and the town’s move hurt their culture and make it harder to keep reindeer. Difficult words: hut (a small, simple house), ore (a natural material in the ground from which people get metal), mine (a place where people take stone or metal from the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Sweden, there is a town called Kiruna. In this town, there is a big red church. The church is very heavy and very old. People build it in 1912. It looks like an old house of the Sámi people. Now the church moves to a new place. It goes slowly, 5 kilometers in two days. The reason for the move is a mine . The mine makes the ground weak . People must move the town because it is safe. Many people come to see the church move. Even the king of Sweden comes. On TV, people can also watch the move. The move costs more than 44 million euros. Some Sámi people are sad and angry. They say that the mine hurts the land, animals, and their life. They say it is bad for reindeer . Difficult words: mine (a place where people take stone or metal from the ground), weak (not strong), reindeer (a large animal which lives in northern parts of Europe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Japan, engineers made a giant humanoid robot looks like something out of a sci-fi movie. It is fixing railway wires that humans cannot reach. JR West and two other companies developed the robot to perform tasks that are considered too high risk for humans. They designed the robot to lower the risk of electrocution and falling, and the company says that the robot reduces human labor by a third. They mounted the robot on a crane , and an engineer controls it through a VR headset and remote controls. The robot can lift up special equipment of up to 40 kilograms in weight to a height of almost ten meters. Currently, maintenance workers use it on out-of-reach railway contact lines in Japan. JR West expects to put it into full service by early 2024. Difficult words: electrocution (an injury or death from electric shock), mounted (fixed), crane (a large tall machine that’s used to move heavy objects). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Japanese engineers are using a giant robot to repair railway wires. JR West and two other companies developed the robot to make workers’ lives safer and easier. The robot can do things which are too dangerous for people. It lowers the risk of electrocution and falls, and it also saves people’s work. The robot is on a crane , and a worker controls it virtually. The robot can lift an object of up to 40 kilograms as high as ten meters. Workers use the robot in difficult areas to reach. By 2024, JR West expects that these robots will help in many places in addition to Japan. Difficult words: giant (very big), electrocution (when electricity hurts or kills someone), crane (a tall machine which moves heavy objects). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Japanese workers use a special robot. It helps fix railway lines . The robot is very big. It can lift things of up to 40 kilograms. It can reach as high as ten meters. The robot does difficult or dangerous work for people. Workers sometimes fall when they fix railway lines. Also, electricity can kill them. The robot helps solve these problems. It saves work, too. The robot is on a crane . It has two hands. A person controls the robot with a remote control and a VR headset . Now, the robot helps only in a few places in Japan. In the near future, it will help in many places. It will help in other countries, too. Difficult words: railway line (the metal tracks that trains move on), crane (a tall machine which moves big objects), VR headset (special glasses or a device which show virtual reality). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Melbourne, researchers have completed Australia’s first clinical trial of psychedelic -assisted therapy for people with terminal illnesses. The study involved 35 participants, who received psilocybin, the active compound in “magic mushrooms” , together with psychotherapy. Results showed significant reductions in depression, anxiety, hopelessness, and psychological distress, while many also experienced reconciliation , forgiveness, and peace when facing death. Although small, the trial has been highly promising. Michael Quinn, a cancer patient, took part and found the treatment helped him manage his fear and frustration, becoming calmer during his final months. However, experts stress that this treatment is not suitable for everyone, especially those with certain psychiatric conditions. Researchers now aim to expand access, though cost and time make the therapy difficult to provide widely. Still, it offers new hope for improving the quality of life. Doctors in Melbourne studied a new treatment for people with serious illnesses. The treatment uses a drug from “magic mushrooms” called psilocybin, together with talking therapy. Thirty-five people joined the trial, and many showed less depression and anxiety . They also felt calmer and more at peace when thinking about death. One patient, Michael Quinn, had cancer and joined the program. His wife Pat said it helped him feel calmer and more relaxed in his last months. Patients usually stayed in quiet rooms, listening to music, and met doctors before and after taking the drug. Experts say the therapy can help some people, but not everyone, especially those with mental health problems. There has to be more research to make it safe and easier for more people. World Mosquito Day, observed on August 20, is not a celebration but a reminder of the serious dangers that mosquitoes pose to global health. The day marks the 1897 discovery by Sir Ronald Ross that mosquitoes transmit malaria, a breakthrough that permanently changed medical science. Despite this milestone, mosquito-borne illnesses still cause enormous harm today, with dengue spreading faster than any other and killing nearly 12,000 people last year. Outbreaks continue into 2025, showing the urgent need for control. Globally, more than one million people die annually due to mosquito-borne diseases. World Mosquito Day urges vigilance , innovation, and united action against these deadly insects. Beth McGraw, a biology professor, stresses that mosquitoes, though tiny, have an extraordinary impact on human health. She points out that prevention at home is critical. Because mosquitoes lay eggs in standing water, eliminating such places, like water collected under pots or around air conditioners, can help reduce their numbers. Difficult words: breakthrough (a sudden discovery or development), dengue (a mosquito-borne disease caused by a virus and common in tropical areas), vigilance (careful watch and attention). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More than one million people die every year from these diseases. The day reminds us to act and to protect life. Difficult words: discover (to find new knowledge), transmit (to carry a disease), act (to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1960, astronomer Frank Drake began the first scientific search for extraterrestrial life at the National Radio Astronomy Observatory in West Virginia, US. Drake aimed a giant antenna at two stars and detected no signals. He wondered how many alien civilizations we could detect, and he estimated 10,000 civilizations had technology or made enough ruckus for us to detect them. Radio telescopes usually measure objects like stars or quasars ; however, they occasionally search frequencies for alien life. In 1995, scientists detected the first planets outside our solar system, and they called them exoplanets. So far, scientists have discovered more than 5,000 exoplanets, and exoplanet Kepler-186f is in the so-called habitable zone where liquid water may support life. People reported many unexplained UFO sightings, and some people believe alien explorers stop at Earth on a galactic road trip. Difficult words: extraterrestrial (from outside Earth), ruckus (a lot of noise), quasar (a very large star that makes a large amount of energy and light). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the 1970s, scientists detected a signal, but it never repeated after that time. Now, scientists focus on exoplanets, which are planets outside our solar system. Some of them are in the right distance from a sun, just like our planet. One of them is Kepler-186f, and scientists hope to find water there. Many people believe that aliens exist, and they visit our planet. People see UFOs sometimes, and they believe that they could be aliens. Difficult words: conclude (to have a result or opinion after thinking about something), detect (to discover that something exists), UFO (a flying object which people can’t explain). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ryan Wardwell, 46, from Long Beach, survived two days trapped behind a waterfall in California’s Seven Teacups. While rappelling down the falls on August 10th, he was thrown off his ropes by extreme hydraulics and forced behind a cascade of the Kern River. When he failed to return to his car that evening, police began searching using drones, infrared equipment, and helicopters. Their first day was unsuccessful due to rough terrain and darkness, but the next day, a drone located him behind the waterfall. Wardwell was alive but exhausted, dehydrated, and stranded in a cold, wet cave. A California Highway Patrol helicopter crew then lifted him to safety in what authorities called a stunning survival story. He was treated for minor injuries and reunited with his family. Video of the dramatic rescue, showing the helicopter struggling against water and foliage , spread widely on social media and news outlets. Officials reminded the public to know their limits when exploring white-water rivers such as the Seven Teacups. Difficult words: rappel (to go down a rock or wall using a rope), hydraulics (the strong force and movement of water), foliage (the leaves of trees and plants). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Wardwell was alive but weak, cold, and very thirsty. He had only small injuries and reunited with his family. Police later shared video of the helicopter rescue, which many people watched online. Authorities called it a stunning survival story and warned visitors to be careful near strong rivers. Difficult words: trapped (unable to get out or escape), rappel (to go down a rock or wall using a rope), cascade (a small waterfall). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Norwich Castle, a 900-year-old Norman fortress , has reopened after a 27.5 million-pound transformation. Built in 1121 by King Henry I, the keep has long dominated Norwich’s skyline as a symbol of Norman power. Now redesigned as The People’s Palace, the Grade I-listed building is considered the UK’s most accessible Norman castle. For the first time in its history, all five floors, from basement to battlements, are open to the public. A new state-of-the-art lift provides access for wheelchair users and families with pushchairs to the rooftop. Inside, visitors can explore carefully recreated Norman royal chambers with authentic furniture, interactive exhibits, and spectacular laser projections in the Great Hall. A new Gallery of Medieval Life, in partnership with the British Museum, displays over 900 medieval artefacts , including 50 long-term loans. Curators highlight Norwich’s importance in the Middle Ages, when it was known as England’s second city thanks to its wealthy wool trade. Difficult words: fortress (a very strong building for defence), authentic (real, not fake), artefact (an old object made by people, often of historical value). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Inside, guests can walk through recreated royal rooms, see interactive displays, and enjoy colorful laser shows in the Great Hall. The new Gallery of Medieval Life shows more than 900 old objects from the British Museum. Experts explain that Norwich was very rich in the Middle Ages, thanks to the wool trade, and people even called it England’s second city. The castle officially reopened on August 13th 2025. Difficult words: fortress (a very strong building), accessible (easy for everyone to get in or use), recreated (newly done, fresh). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A highly anticipated summit took place in Anchorage, Alaska, where President Trump and President Putin met for almost three hours. Many had hoped for a breakthrough on Ukraine, and Trump even stood in front of a banner reading ‘Pursuing Peace.’ However, when the meeting ended, Trump gave no details and ignored reporters. This vague message suggested some progress, but nothing concrete had been achieved. For Putin, simply sitting with the US president was already a success. Since the war began in 2022, Western governments have tried to isolate him. This meeting broke that image and showed Russia was still part of global diplomacy. At the same time, the US signaled strength with a bomber flyover during the leaders’ walk. Trump later said he wouldn’t sanction Russia directly but would pressure its buyers, such as India and China, to keep influence. In the end, Trump told Zelensky to make a deal, showing he sees Ukraine as weaker. The summit gave Putin a symbolic victory but left Ukraine uncertain. Difficult words: vague (unclear, not definite), concrete (clear, specific), signal (to show something, often without words). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US also showed its power with a bomber flying above during the summit. Later, Trump said he wouldn’t punish Russia directly. Instead, he wanted to put pressure on countries like India and China that buy Russian oil. Finally, Trump advised President Zelensky to make a deal, making clear he thinks Russia is the stronger side. Difficult words: progress (moving closer to a goal), confused (not able to understand or think clearly), bomber (a big military plane with bombs). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An animal lover in Jordan spends thousands of dinars every month to feed stray dogs, as he posts videos online to encourage Jordanians to follow in his footsteps. Nader Abd al-Raheem al-Morshed spends around 1,400 dollars every month to feed and vaccinate abandoned street dogs as part of an initiative that he started seven years ago. His main goal is to change people’s outlook on dogs, so that they can live with the animals peacefully. People often think that it is necessary to get rid of these dogs, who are often uncared-for or left sick in the street. Morshed recently started to upload videos of the dogs on Tik Tok; these are videos he created for many years before Tik Tok even existed. He does this to make people aware that dogs were pets and they were friendly and good with people. He hopes to inspire others to do the same and to prevent the dogs from eating each other or waiting for each other to die. Difficult words: stray (having no home or having wandered away from home), initiative (an action to resolve a difficulty or improve a situation), uncared-for (not receiving enough care or attention). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: vaccinate (to give a person or animal a vaccine which stops them from getting a disease), abandoned (when someone is without the care or help of others), get rid (to throw away or destroy something that you no longer want). Petunia won the title at the ‘World’s Ugliest Dog Contest,’ held at the Sonoma County Fair in California. She and her owner, Shannon Nyman, received 5,000 dollars and the right to brag about their success. This contest has been around for nearly fifty years, proving that a dog’s breed or appearance doesn’t define its value. The competition celebrates dogs with unusual looks and personalities. Many of the dogs in the contest come from shelters or puppy mills , which means they have been rescued. This shows how adoption can give pets a second chance for a happy life. The contest helps people understand the importance of saving animals and appreciating their unique qualities. The event is more than just a competition. It is a celebration of diversity among dogs that encourages kindness towards all animals, no matter how they look. Petunia’s victory shows that being different can be special. Difficult words: brag (to talk about yourself or something you did in a way that shows you want others to be impressed), breed (a group of animals, especially dogs, that share similar looks and traits because they come from the same family line), puppy mill (a place where dogs are kept and bred in poor conditions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
